newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan forex turnover rises in November.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan forex turnover rises in November.

text.p: Average daily turnover on Taiwan's foreign exchange market rose 5.2 percent to US$4.237 billion in November from a year earlier, the central bank said on Monday.
Of the average daily total, 23 percent was between the U.S. dollar and yen while 11.2 percent was dollar-deutschemark trade.
Trade between the Taiwan dollar and the U.S. dollar accounted for 37.2 percent while trade of the Taiwan dollar against other foreign currencies trade made up 3.3 percent.
Spot trading comprised 66.2 percent of the total, cross-currency swaps 14.2 percent, margin trading 11 percent, forward trading 7.3 percent and options 1.3 percent.

Compared with November 1995, November 1996 spot trade turnover was up 1.8 percent, cross-currency swaps fell 14.2 percent, margin trading surged 84.2 percent, forward trading jumped 63.1 percent and options trading rose 42.9 percent.
Interbank trading conducted through brokers typically amounted to less than 10 percent of daily total trade, a central bank official said.
Other transactions included direct interbank trading and trade between banks and clients, he said.

Taiwan, which started financial derivatives trading in early 1994, allows more than 10 derivatives to be traded, including cross-currency swaps, and margin, options and interest rate swaps trading, the bank said in a statement.
